summary.text: Mujtaba Mohammed is a Democratic member of the North Carolina State Senate who has represented District 38 since January 2019 and is on the ballot for re-election on November 3, 2026.
He is a public interest attorney.

paragraphs.text: Mujtaba Mohammed was born in Toledo, Ohio, according to Ballotpedia.

He earned a bachelor's degree from the University of North Carolina at Charlotte and a J.D. from the North Carolina Central University School of Law, and his professional experience includes working as a public interest attorney.

In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as a longtime Charlotte resident born in the United States to immigrant parents from India, and said he was appointed by Governor Roy Cooper to the North Carolina Council on Developmental Disabilities and the state's Task Force for Racial Equity in Criminal Justice.
Mohammed was elected to the Senate in 2018, according to his survey, and Ballotpedia lists him as assuming office on January 1, 2019, as the successor to Joel Ford.
For 2025-2026, Ballotpedia lists his committee assignments as Appropriations on Justice and Public Safety, Health Care, Judiciary, Transportation and Finance.
In the 2022 survey, he said his priorities include quality public schools, investments in families and affordable access to health care.
